title: Parsing a triple-encoded input
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and let $y$ be a finite bit string. Either there are bit strings $x,w,w'$ and natural numbers $s,q_1,\mathrm{cap}$ such that $y=\langle x,\langle w,\langle w',\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle\rangle$, the binary expansion of $s$ has length at most the length of the binary expansion of $|y|$, and $q_1,\mathrm{cap}\le (8W+8)(|y|+1)$, where $W$ is the machine-dependent width defined for $N$. In this case the step-mode program reaches its $N_1$ copy stage from its initial length scan, with all registers bounded by $(8W+8)(|y|+1)$ at every earlier step, and with register values $L=|y|$, $P=2|x|+2|w|+2|w'|+6$, $A=2|x|+2$, $B=2|x|+2|w|+4$, $Q_1=q_1$, $\mathrm{Cap}=\mathrm{cap}$, $Q_2=2|x|+2|w|+2|w'|+6$, and $S=s$ at that stage. Otherwise, if no such triple and $s$ satisfy the encoding and binary-length condition, the program halts with answer false from its initial length scan, with all registers bounded by the same bound at every earlier step.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean input
